text:
olivia: quick q — trying to move inference-service in `inference-prod` from ALB TLS termination to NLB TLS passthrough to preserve client certs and reduce latency. planning a canary. any pitfalls we should check?
sam: sounds reasonable. main things: healthcheck port/method, externalTrafficPolicy, and how the TLS secret is bound to the NLB target. also session affinity if you need client IP.
jia: +1. specifically watch readinessProbe != service.targetPort mismatches — k8s will route healthchecks to nodeport vs target and ALB vs NLB behavior differs.
olivia: good call. current service YAML is simple svc type: LoadBalancer. attaching snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-service
  namespace: inference-prod
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol: "*" # we might need to remove if passthrough
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
    - name: https
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8080
      protocol: TCP
  selector:
    app: inference
```
sam: for TLS passthrough with NLB you want to avoid proxy protocol unless you unwrap TLS. if you need client IP in app, set externalTrafficPolicy: Local and NodePort + hostNetwork options considered. for healthchecks: NLB expects an instance target type health check (tcp) unless you use ALB. make sure your readiness probe listens on targetPort 8080 for TCP/TLS or expose a plain http health endpoint on another port if possible.
matt: about secret wiring — we currently use certs in k8s secret `inference-tls`. With passthrough the NLB needs the cert if terminating TLS, but for passthrough the cert stays on the pod. so we don't attach the secret to the LB. confirm we don't try to bind that secret in terraform/annotations.
jia: yep. if terraform has an `aws_lb_listener_certificate` or `aws_lb_listener` expecting ACM cert, that would imply termination at LB. check the infra repo for any listener resources.
olivia: infra PR is up: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4822 — it changes service annotations + tf to switch lb type and adds `external_traffic_policy = "Local"` in the helm values. can someone review quick?
sam: looking. one quick pointer: update the health check doc in the helm chart values to set `health.path: /ready` and `health.port: 8080`. otherwise node-level TCP checks might cycle.
matt: small terraform note — we previously created a TG with target type `ip`. NLB passthrough wants target type `instance` for k8s nodeport targets unless using target group binding. double-check `aws_lb_target_group` in the PR.
infra-bot: CI passed for infra/pr/4822 (plan ok).
olivia: thanks. also question about canary: plan to roll 10% traffic via gateway route weighting. Is Gateway API route supported for NLB passthrough?
jia: Gateway API supports passthrough with TCPRoutes or TLSRoutes depending on controller. For us, we use AWS NLB + gateway-controller. You can create a TLSRoute with passthrough action. make sure SNI is set if you need multi-host.
sam: on SNI — with passthrough the NLB won't inspect hostname unless using TLS listener with SNI proxying and multiple backends. if you need SNI routing, you probably want ALB or a TLS listener that terminates at LB and re-mtls to pods.
matt: For canary, I recommend: 1) deploy new svc annotated NLB in a canary namespace with same targetPort and readiness; 2) create a Gateway/TLSRoute with weight 10 to canary; 3) run load tests and run `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername example.com` against the NLB IP to validate passthrough; 4) watch health checks and node logs.
olivia: noted. one last wiring question — terraform currently references a secret arn in a variable `tls_cert_arn`. if we switch to passthrough we should null that var to avoid creating an LB listener. can someone add a guard in PR?
sam: I can add a conditional in terraform: `count = var.tls_cert_arn != "" ? 1 : 0` on the aws_lb_listener_certificate resource. will add in next commit.
matt: I'll update helm values to expose a non-TLS health endpoint on 8081 at `/healthz` so NLB TCP checks can hit plain tcp and apps won't need to decrypt. simple change.
olivia: perfect. thanks all. tagging @matt and @sam for follow-ups. deploying a preview when infra PR merged — please post when ready. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Preview env created: https://preview.redwood.dev/inference-canary (expires in 24h).
